annotations.text:
Same pages, same order, same minimalism — a coherent shell around them.

What's new:
• A real app bar: grouped nav (Watch / Manage), active-page marker, and the verdict pip carried on EVERY page.
• Page bands: a title plus one sentence saying what the page is for.
• Section rules instead of a run of h3/h4.
• Tabular mono for every number.
• Cards on surfaces, hairlines everywhere else.

The one real departure: the verdict banner is now a tinted card with an accent edge rather than a full-bleed colour slab. Compare the two dashboards — if you want the slab back it's a one-line change.

Dark mode is chosen, not flipped.

The chrome takes Pico's own dark tokens. The incident ramp could not just be inverted: your grey ramp ends at #2b2b2b, which is invisible on a #13161f page.

So in dark the grey ramp runs dark → near-white instead of pale → black. 'Deeper = worse' still holds, it just runs toward light. The warm ramp keeps its direction, so warm-vs-grey separation survives at every tier.

History is shown in dark on purpose: the punchcard and the ribbon board are where that decision either works or doesn't.

Phone: 390px, the full scrolling page (not a viewport crop).

• Nav collapses to the drawer; the verdict pip stays in the bar, because knowing the verdict is why the page is open.
• Tree rows grow to 44px and drop the address — it lives on Targets.
• The glitch table restacks as cards; tables don't survive 390px.
• Theme choice (Light / Dark / System) lives in the drawer footer with the build stamp.

One thing to decide: I surfaced each target's IP next to its name on the desktop tree, where today it's only a tooltip. Easy to drop if it's noise.
